subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following parts controls the amount of light entering the eye by influencing the size of the pupil?
A Sclera
B Cornea
C Retina
D Iris
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The iris is the coloured, muscular ring of the eye. Its radial and circular muscles adjust the size of the pupil, controlling the amount of light entering the eye.

subQuestions.questionText:
The function of the umbilical vein is to transport …
A carbon dioxide from the foetus to the mother.
B nutrients from the foetus to the mother.
C carbon dioxide from the mother to the foetus.
D nutrients from the mother to the foetus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The umbilical vein carries oxygenated, nutrient-rich blood from the placenta (mother) to the foetus. The umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated, waste-laden blood from the foetus to the placenta.

options.A: carbon dioxide from the foetus to the mother.
options.B: nutrients from the foetus to the mother.
options.C: carbon dioxide from the mother to the foetus.
options.D: nutrients from the mother to the foetus.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram below represents the events that occur during the homeostatic control of blood glucose. Gland X detects the change, the level of glucose in blood decreases, the level of hormone Y increases, and the level of glucose in blood then increases.
Which ONE of the following represents gland X and hormone Y?
A Gland X: Pancreas; Hormone Y: Glucagon
B Gland X: Pituitary; Hormone Y: Glucagon
C Gland X: Pancreas; Hormone Y: Insulin
D Gland X: Pituitary; Hormone Y: Insulin
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
A drop in blood glucose is detected by the pancreas, which secretes glucagon. Glucagon raises blood glucose, so gland X is the pancreas and hormone Y is glucagon.

options.A: Gland X: Pancreas; Hormone Y: Glucagon
options.B: Gland X: Pituitary; Hormone Y: Glucagon
options.C: Gland X: Pancreas; Hormone Y: Insulin
options.D: Gland X: Pituitary; Hormone Y: Insulin

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is CORRECT regarding the homeostatic control of the carbon dioxide concentration in the blood?
A The lungs have receptors.
B High oxygen levels is the stimulus.
C Breathing muscles are the effectors.
D The process is controlled by the cerebrum.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
In the control of blood carbon dioxide, the breathing (intercostal and diaphragm) muscles act as the effectors that change the rate and depth of breathing. The stimulus is a high CO2 level, receptors are in the aorta/carotid arteries and the process is controlled by the medulla oblongata, not the cerebrum.

options.B: High oxygen levels is the stimulus.
options.D: The process is controlled by the cerebrum.

subQuestions.questionText:
The plant hormones that can be used to kill broad-leaved weeds are …
A abscisic acid only.
B abscisic acid and gibberellins.
C auxins only.
D abscisic acid and auxins.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Synthetic auxins are used as selective herbicides that cause uncontrolled growth in broad-leaved (dicotyledonous) weeds, killing them while leaving narrow-leaved crops unharmed.

subQuestions.questionText:
A girl looking at a car moving away from her is able to focus on the letters on the number plate.
Which ONE of the following changes occurred in her eyes?
A The suspensory ligaments slackened.
B The ciliary muscles relaxed.
C Light rays were refracted more.
D The lens became more convex.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
For distant objects the ciliary muscles relax, the suspensory ligaments become taut, and the lens is pulled thin (less convex) so that light is refracted less. This is accommodation for distant vision.

subQuestions.questionText:
One of the characteristics of a sperm that causes it to move faster is the …
A oval-shaped head.
B haploid nucleus.
C presence of enzymes in the acrosome.
D absence of a middle piece.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The streamlined, oval-shaped head reduces resistance and allows the sperm to swim faster. The acrosome enzymes penetrate the ovum, the haploid nucleus carries genes, and the middle piece (which is present) provides energy.

options.C: presence of enzymes in the acrosome.

subQuestions.questionText:
In a person suffering from long-sightedness, …
A the eyeball is longer than normal.
B light rays fall behind the retina.
C light rays are refracted more by the lens.
D distant objects will appear blurred.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
In long-sightedness (hypermetropia) the eyeball is too short (or the lens too weak), so light rays converge to a focus behind the retina and near objects appear blurred.

options.A: the eyeball is longer than normal.
options.B: light rays fall behind the retina.
options.C: light rays are refracted more by the lens.

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph below shows the results of an investigation done to determine the effect of light intensity on the size of the pupil. The graph plots size of pupil (mm) against distance from the light source (cm).
Which ONE of the following statements is a conclusion that can be made from the results?
A As the distance from the light source increases, the size of the pupil increases.
B As the distance from the light source decreases, the size of the pupil increases.
C As the size of the pupil increases, the distance from the light source increases.
D As the size of the pupil decreases, the distance from the light source increases.
(Refer to the graph in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
As the distance from the light source increases, light intensity decreases, so the pupil dilates and its size increases. The conclusion must be phrased with the independent variable (distance) as the cause and pupil size as the effect.

options.A: As the distance from the light source increases, the size of the pupil increases.
options.B: As the distance from the light source decreases, the size of the pupil increases.
options.C: As the size of the pupil increases, the distance from the light source increases.
options.D: As the size of the pupil decreases, the distance from the light source increases.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is a list of events that occur in the female body:
(i) Puberty
(ii) Ovulation
(iii) Development of the corpus luteum
(iv) Oogenesis
(v) Thickening of the endometrium
Which ONE of the following is a combination of events that are influenced by LH (luteinising hormone)?
A (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) and (v)
B (ii), (iii), (iv) and (v) only
C (ii) and (iii) only
D (iii) only
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A surge in LH triggers ovulation (ii) and stimulates the development of the corpus luteum (iii). Puberty, oogenesis and the thickening of the endometrium are influenced by other hormones (e.g. oestrogen/FSH).

subQuestions.memoText: Placenta (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The pigmented layer of the eye that absorbs excess light.
subQuestions.memoText: Choroid (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The part of a neuron that plays a role in the speed at which a nerve impulse is transmitted.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The part of the male reproductive system which temporarily stores sperm until they mature.
subQuestions.memoText: Epididymis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.
Description: A process that produces four mature gametes in humans from a single diploid cell.
A: Oogenesis
B: Spermatogenesis
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
Spermatogenesis produces four mature, functional sperm cells from a single diploid cell. Oogenesis produces only one mature ovum (plus polar bodies) from a single diploid cell.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.
Description: A defence mechanism that protects plants against herbivores.
A: Thorns
B: Chemicals
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Both thorns (physical/structural defence) and chemicals (chemical defence) protect plants against herbivores.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.
Description: The nerve that transmits impulses from the retina to the brain.
A: Optic nerve
B: Auditory nerve
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
The optic nerve transmits impulses from the retina to the brain. The auditory nerve transmits impulses from the ear (cochlea) to the brain.

subQuestions.questionText:
In some frog species, during mating, the male climbs onto the back of the female and grasps her with his front legs. During this time, the female will release about 6 000 ova, while the male releases sperm onto them. This mating behaviour is called amplexus.
Name the type of fertilisation that occurs during reproduction in frogs.
subQuestions.memoText: External fertilisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: With reference to the frog (amplexus) reproduction above, explain why the fertilised eggs of these frogs do not survive on land.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
Mark 1: The eggs will dry out
Mark 2: because they have no shells / are not amniotic eggs / have no amnion

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how amplexus increases the chances of fertilisation in frogs.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 x 2 = 2 marks). Mark the first ONE only:
Option 1: The male and female bodies are in close contact (1) so that sperm can be released directly onto the ova (1)
OR
Option 2: Many / up to 6 000 ova are released (1) since fertilisation is external (1)

subQuestions.questionText: From the information above, explain ONE other strategy that contributes to the reproductive success of the frog species.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 x 2 = 2 marks). Mark the first ONE only:
Option 1: Many / up to 6 000 ova are released (1) since fertilisation is external / increasing the chance that some will be fertilised (1)
OR
Option 2: The male and female bodies are in close contact (1) so that sperm can be released directly onto the ova (1)

The diagram below represents the male reproductive system, with part A and the prostate gland labelled, and part B lying near the prostate gland. Name:
(a) Part A
(b) The hormone secreted by B
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Part A – Seminal vesicle (1 mark)
(b) Testosterone (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE function of the fluid secreted by the prostate gland during reproduction.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 x 2 = 2 marks). Mark the first ONE only:
Option 1: It is alkaline (1) to neutralise the acidic conditions of the vagina (1)
Option 2: It contains mucus / provides medium (1) to facilitate the movement of the sperm (1)
Option 3: It contains nutrients (1) to supply the sperm with energy (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Prostate cancer is one of the most common types of cancer among men. The table below shows the number of men per 100 000 men of different age groups that were diagnosed with prostate cancer in a certain country over a period of 14 years.
Age group | Number of prostate cancer cases (per 100 000 men)
<49 | 5
50–54 | 135
55–59 | 288
60–64 | 488
65–69 | 720
70–74 | 764
75–79 | 693
>80 | 473
(a) According to the table, which age group of men is most likely to develop prostate cancer?
(b) Draw a histogram to represent the data for men from the age group 60–64 to the age group 75–79.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 70–74 (1 mark)

(b) Criteria for marking the histogram (6 marks):
• Histogram is drawn (T) – 1
• Caption of the graph includes both variables (C) – 1
• Correct labels on the X-axis and Y-axis with correct unit on the Y-axis (L) – 1
• Correct scale for Y-axis AND bars of equal width with no spaces for X-axis (S) – 1
• Plotting (P) correctly done for: 1–3 age groups = 1; all 4 required age groups only = 2

Note: If a bar graph or line graph is drawn, marks are lost for the type of graph and the scale. If axes are transposed: candidate can get all marks if labels are also swopped and bars are horizontal; if labels are not corresponding then marks are lost for labels and scale, but plotting can get credit if the coordinates are correct for the given labels.

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the extract about ovarian cysts. Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled structures that develop inside the ovaries of some women. The two most common types of cysts in women of reproductive age are follicular cysts and corpus luteum cysts. Follicular cysts develop when a Graafian follicle fails to rupture and release the ovum; the follicle continues to grow because of continued hormonal stimulation. A corpus luteum cyst develops when the corpus luteum does not degenerate, even when a person is not pregnant. Women often show no symptoms and the cysts disappear, but in rare cases ovarian cysts keep on increasing in size. A very large cyst can cause intense pain and may rupture, leading to internal bleeding, and will require surgical removal.
From the extract, give:
(a) TWO structures in the ovary that may develop into cysts
(b) TWO symptoms associated with very large cysts
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (Mark the first TWO only):
• (Graafian) follicle
• Corpus luteum (2 marks)
(b) (Mark the first TWO only):
• (Intense) pain
• Internal bleeding (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
With reference to the ovarian cyst extract, name the hormone:
(a) Responsible for the growth of the follicle under normal conditions
(b) That will be high in concentration in the blood of women where follicular cysts develop
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) FSH (1 mark)
(b) Oestrogen OR LH OR FSH (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.3.2(b).
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark) Any ONE of the following:
• The Graafian follicle keeps on producing oestrogen / fails to rupture
OR
• The increased secretion of oestrogen stimulates the secretion of LH
OR
• Excess production of FSH can cause the failure to ovulate / the Graafian follicle to rupture

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why a woman will not be able to fall pregnant if she has a corpus luteum cyst that does not disappear.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5 of the following (5 marks):
• The corpus luteum does not degenerate and
• keeps on secreting progesterone
• This will inhibit the pituitary gland
• from secreting FSH
• Therefore no follicle will develop and
• no ovulation will take place

subQuestions.questionText:
A learner suffered a brain injury during a rugby match. He could still breathe properly but he experienced occasional loss of memory and balance. Refer to the diagram of the central nervous system and explain why:
(a) The learner could still breathe properly
(b) It is possible that the injury affected part B
(c) The hearing of the learner could also be affected because of the injury
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (2 marks)
• Part D / medulla oblongata which controls breathing
• was not injured
(b) (2 marks)
• The learner (occasionally) lost balance
• due to no coordination of voluntary movements by part B
(c) (2 marks)
• The loss of memory indicates a possible injury to part A / the cerebrum
• which is also responsible for hearing / (interpretation of) sound

subQuestions.questionText:
The efficiency and speed of the knee-jerk reaction is very important for balance and movement. The stimulation of the patellar tendon, just below the knee cap (patella), causes the contraction and relaxation of the quadriceps muscle in the upper leg. A diagram represents the reflex arc for the knee-jerk reaction containing only ONE synapse; the arrows indicate the transmission of nerve impulses.
What is a reflex action?
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
• A rapid, involuntary / automatic response
• to a stimulus

subQuestions.questionText:
With reference to the knee-jerk reflex, state:
(a) ONE reason why a synapse is significant
(b) The importance of the knee-jerk reaction
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) It ensures that the impulse is transmitted in one direction (1 mark). (Mark the first ONE only.)
(b) It is important for balance / movement (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Describe the pathway of the impulse in this reflex arc to bring about the knee-jerk reaction.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(5 marks) (Correct sequence is required):
• The impulse is transmitted from the receptors in the patellar tendon through the
• sensory neuron and the
• synapse to the
• motor neuron and to the
• quadriceps muscle

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the extract about Alzheimer's disease and exercise. Age and family history are the known risk factors for Alzheimer's disease. The most common symptom of Alzheimer's disease is a worsening ability to remember new information. Regular exercise may help to reduce the risk of developing Alzheimer's disease because it can improve blood flow to the brain and help to maintain the volume of the hippocampus. The hippocampus is located deep inside the cerebrum and plays a major role in learning ability and orientation. Scientists conducted an investigation to determine if regular exercise reduces the risk of Alzheimer's disease in humans. They used 37 female participants between the ages of 65 and 75 in an exercise programme; used participants that did not show symptoms of Alzheimer's disease at the start of the investigation; and conducted the investigation three times a week for three months. The results showed an improvement in higher-order thinking abilities and an increased blood flow to the cerebrum.
State ONE change in the nerve tissue of the brain that can cause Alzheimer's disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark) Any ONE of the following (Mark the first ONE only):
• Degeneration / wasting away of nerve tissue
• Plaque / proteins formed around the nerve tissue

subQuestions.questionText:
From the Alzheimer's extract, state:
(a) ONE symptom of Alzheimer's disease
(b) A genetic risk factor
(c) TWO functions of the hippocampus
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Worsening ability to remember new information (1 mark). (Mark the first ONE only.)
(b) Family history (1 mark)
(c) (Mark the first TWO only):
• Learning ability
• Orientation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO factors that were considered when selecting the participants for this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks) They (Mark the first TWO only):
• Were all females / considered gender
• Were between the ages of 65 and 75 / considered age group / age
• Did not show symptoms of Alzheimer's disease

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the scientists improved the reliability of their results.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks) They (Mark the first TWO only):
• Used 37 participants
• Conducted the investigation three times a week
• Conducted the investigation for three months

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why this investigation cannot be used to conclude that exercise reduces the risk of getting Alzheimer's disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 x 2 = 2 marks) Any ONE of the following pairs:
Option 1: The investigation did not establish the relationship between exercise and the development of Alzheimer's disease (1) since no changes in the nervous tissue were measured / the period was short (1)
Option 2: There was no control group (1) to show that it is the exercise that improves blood flow / higher-order thinking abilities (1)
Option 3: People who did not show symptoms of Alzheimer's disease were used (1) therefore, the results do not show prevention of the development of Alzheimer's disease (1)

subQuestions.questionText: From the extract, explain why it is expected that regular exercise can reduce the risk of Alzheimer's disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
• Exercise can improve blood flow to the brain and
• it can maintain the volume of the hippocampus which will
• prevent a decrease in higher-order thinking / cognitive abilities / learning abilities

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram below shows the location of the adrenal gland in the human body, with the adrenal gland and organ X labelled. Identify:
(a) Organ X
(b) The system to which the adrenal gland belongs
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Organ X – Kidney (1 mark)
(b) Endocrine system (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO characteristics of the type of glands that belongs to the system identified in QUESTION 3.2.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks) (Mark the first TWO only):
• It releases hormones
• directly into the blood / and it is ductless

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the interaction between the adrenal gland and organ X in maintaining homeostasis when salt levels in the blood are low.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5 of the following (5 marks):
• Low salt levels are detected by receptor cells in the kidney
• Adrenal glands are stimulated to secrete
• more aldosterone
• which stimulates the renal tubules
• to be more permeable to salt
• This increases the reabsorption of salt and
• the salt levels in the blood increase / return back to normal

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the effect that a secretion of the pituitary gland will have on organ X when a person experiences dehydration.
subQuestions.memoText:
(5 marks)
• The secretion of ADH
• will increase
• which will increase the permeability
• of the renal tubules in X
• so that more water is reabsorbed from the filtrate

subQuestions.questionText:
A twelve-year-old boy participated in physical exercise for 45 minutes, followed by a 15-minute rest period. The skin temperature of the boy was measured and the results were recorded. A diagram represents the skin of the boy before exercise (with parts P and Q labelled), and a graph shows the changes in skin temperature: 37,4 °C before exercise, 35,4 °C directly after exercise, and 36,9 °C after a rest period.
Name the:
(a) Homeostatic mechanism that brings about the change in skin temperature
(b) Part of the brain that is responsible for the mechanism named in QUESTION 3.3.1(a)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Thermoregulation (1 mark)
(b) Hypothalamus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
From the diagram of the boy's skin, identify the following parts:
(a) P
(b) Q
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) P – Sweat gland (1 mark)
(b) Q – Capillary / blood vessel (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage decrease in the average skin temperature of the boy before and directly after exercise. Show ALL working. (Skin temperature was 37,4 °C before exercise and 35,4 °C directly after exercise.)

Explain the roles of part P and part Q in the change in skin temperature from before exercise to directly after exercise.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(6 marks)
• Skin temperature decreased / lowered from 37,4 ºC to 35,4 ºC
• because part Q dilated / vasodilated
• causing more blood to flow to the (surface of the) skin and
• part P became (more) active / produced more sweat
• causing more heat to be lost to the environment
• through evaporation / radiation / convection

subQuestions.questionText:
An investigation was done to determine the effect of auxins on the growth of lateral branches. (The elongation of lateral buds results in the growth of lateral branches.) The procedure was as follows: Four potted plants (A, B, C and D) of the same species were used. Plant A was left untreated. The apical bud of plant B was removed. The apical bud of plant C was removed and replaced with agar jelly (a jelly-like substance through which other substances can diffuse). The apical bud of plant D was removed and replaced with agar jelly containing auxins. The plants were exposed to the same environmental conditions. The length of the lateral buds of each plant was measured at the beginning of the investigation and again after three weeks.
Results – Length of the lateral buds (mm):
Plant A: at the beginning 7,0; after three weeks 7,3
Plant B: at the beginning 6,9; after three weeks 10,4
Plant C: at the beginning 7,2; after three weeks 10,3
Plant D: at the beginning 7,1; after three weeks 7,2
For this investigation, state the:
(a) Independent variable
(b) Dependent variable
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (Presence / absence of) auxins (1 mark)
(b) Growth of lateral branches (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: With reference to the auxin investigation, explain why all the plants were exposed to the same environmental conditions.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
• To ensure that the results are caused only by the presence of auxins which
• increases the validity of the investigation

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why agar without auxins was used in plant C.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 of the following (3 marks):
• It acts as a control
• to show that the results of Plant D
• are caused by the (presence of) auxins
• and not the agar jelly

subQuestions.questionText: State a conclusion for this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks) Any ONE of the following:
• The presence of auxins slows down the growth of lateral branches
OR
• The absence of auxins stimulated the growth of lateral branches
